what: How each North Dakota place voted in six contests of the 2020, 2022 and 2024 general elections: the votes for the Democratic-NPL ticket, the Republican ticket, everyone else together (write-ins included) and the total, added up from the North Dakota Secretary of State's official precinct results.
note: What this is: how the people of a place voted in that election, in the precinct results the county auditors and the Secretary of State publish, added up here by county, by judicial district and, for 2022 and 2024, by legislative district, on the precinct and district lines in force at that election. What this is not: it is not a prediction of any election; it says nothing about any candidate on a later ballot or about any voter; a nonpartisan office stays nonpartisan (every county office in North Dakota is one); and a place is not its lines for ever: where a district was drawn again, the figures are for the lines of that year. The tickets are named, as the Secretary's own results name them, only to say which election this was. In a place with very few voters the split would come close to saying how particular people voted; those contests are listed in the place's too_few, and a page should leave the split out.
how_to_read: Each place's votes are four counts for each contest: dem (the Democratic-NPL ticket), rep (the Republican ticket), other (every other candidate and all write-ins) and total. Minnesota's file calls the first count dfl. A contest a place does not have was not counted on its lines: legislative districts are given for 2022 and 2024 only.

too_few.why: A place's too_few lists the contests in which it had fewer than 20 votes, or in which every vote went the same way. There the split comes close to saying how particular people voted, so a page should leave it out. The counts are the official record all the same, and are kept here so that the sums can be checked.

county.key: five-digit county FIPS code, as sl_places kind county and the jurisdiction_id of our county races

senate.key: district number, as the jurisdiction_id of our Senate races
senate.why_not_2020: The 2020 election was held on the districts drawn after the 2010 census, and its precincts are not numbered by district; the districts drawn after the 2020 census were first used in 2022, so 2020 is not given.
senate.note: A precinct's district is the third and fourth digits of its number. Each year is on the lines in force at that election. Districts 9, 15 reach different counties in the 2022 and the 2024 results, so the lines there were drawn again between the two elections; a change inside a county would not show in this comparison. These files do not say which lines a later election uses.

house.key: district number, as the jurisdiction_id of our House races
house.why_not_2020: The 2020 election was held on the districts drawn after the 2010 census, and its precincts are not numbered by district; the districts drawn after the 2020 census were first used in 2022, so 2020 is not given.
house.note: A precinct's district is the third and fourth digits of its number. Each year is on the lines in force at that election. Districts 9, 15 reach different counties in the 2022 and the 2024 results, so the lines there were drawn again between the two elections; a change inside a county would not show in this comparison. These files do not say which lines a later election uses. The figures are the whole district's, the same as under senate; House subdistricts (4A, 4B) are not given apart.

judicial.key: ND- and the district's letters (ND-EC), as sl_places kind judicial_district
judicial.note: The counties of each district are those that voted in its judicial contests at the 2022 general election; every year's figures are those counties' votes.

control.statement: For every contest the precinct rows add up to the official statewide totals named here and, county by county, to the Secretary's own county report for each of the 53 counties; in every county sheet the precincts add up to the sheet's TOTALS row; and counties, legislative districts and judicial districts each add up to the statewide sum.

notes: For Governor the statewide control is the TOTALS row of the Secretary's own county report, a second report of the same results system and not an independent document; President and U.S. Senator are checked against the Clerk of the U.S. House's statistics.
The precinct and county workbooks of 2022 and 2020 call themselves 'Unofficial' in their first line; the pages they are exported from are headed Official. Both are recorded under sources.

coverage.not_given: Cities and townships: a North Dakota precinct is numbered, often takes in several townships and cities, and the results do not say which. Soil conservation districts: some share a county, and the results do not say which precincts are in which. School districts and county commissioner districts: the precinct results do not name them. House subdistricts (4A, 4B): the precinct number carries the district only. Legislative districts for 2020: other lines, and precincts not numbered by district.
